action_history.rationale: Model: Sum of 10 Voigt profiles on flat near-zero baseline with stiff-ALS (lam=1e7) residual-offset removal; low-wavenumber cluster re-partitioned into narrow 143/190/214 components (214 dominant), 1085 main+narrow-apex dual component to remove derivative oscillation; 1/sqrt(y)-weighted Levenberg-Marquardt over full range

result.detailed_analysis: Band summary (center cm-1, relative intensity, strongest first): 1085 (1.00, ν1 CO3 symmetric stretch, comprising the merged 1083/1085 dual component), 213 (0.41, lattice/translational mode), 1238 (0.68 broad) and 1206 (0.40 broad) (high-wavenumber cluster), 701 (0.37) + 706 (0.16) (ν4 in-plane bend doublet), 190 (0.31, lattice), 277 (0.25, lattice), 143 (0.03, low-frequency lattice). The dominant sharp ν1 near 1085 cm-1 with a resolved ~701/705 ν4 doublet is the diagnostic fingerprint of ARAGONITE (orthorhombic CaCO3): aragonite shows ν1 ~1085, a characteristic 705+701 ν4 doublet, and lattice modes near 206 and 152. Calcite is disfavored because calcite exhibits a single ν4 near 712 cm-1 and its strongest lattice modes near 282 and 156, and dolomite is excluded because its ν1 sits at ~1097 cm-1 (not 1085). The measured lattice modes (143, 190, 213, 277) are broadly consistent with the aragonite/CaCO3 lattice-mode envelope, with 213 being the strongest low-frequency band as expected for the aragonite translational region. The broad 1206/1238 cluster is not a standard carbonate fundamental; it may arise from ν3 antisymmetric-stretch activity, a combination/overtone region, an organic/biogenic matrix component (common in biogenic aragonite), or a fitting artifact absorbing baseline curvature — it is the least secure assignment. The 1085 apex residual (derivative-shaped, >3 sigma) indicates the true ν1 is asymmetric/very sharp and slightly under-resolved by symmetric Voigts; this does not change the phase ID but means the split into two 1083/1085 components is a fitting device rather than evidence of two carbonate environments. Overall the pattern (strongest three bands: 1085, 213, and the 701/706 doublet plus 1238 broad) is well explained as aragonite, an identification made on band pattern alone since no elemental chemistry was provided.

scientific_claims.claim: The spectrum is identified as aragonite (orthorhombic CaCO3), diagnosed by the ν1 symmetric stretch at 1085.2 cm-1 together with a resolved ν4 in-plane-bend doublet at 701.2 and 705.7 cm-1 and lattice modes at ~213/190/277 cm-1; the ν4 doublet and 1085 (vs. calcite's single ~712 and dolomite's ~1097) separate the CaCO3 polymorph.
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: Distinguishing aragonite from calcite by Raman lineshape is central to biomineralization, paleoclimate/paleoenvironment reconstruction, and diagenetic studies, where polymorph identity encodes formation temperature and biological control; the resolved ν4 doublet is the definitive discriminator.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone confirmed aragonite versus calcite assignment using the resolved ν4 doublet near 701/705 cm-1 alongside the ν1 at 1085 cm-1 in Raman spectra?

verification_iterations.model: Sum of Voigt profiles on a flat/near-zero linear baseline with stiff-ALS residual-offset removal. Components (10 total): (1) ~190, (2) ~215, (3) ~272, (4) ~284 (doublet partner, 241-312 region), (5) ~701, (6) ~706 (doublet partner, 685-721 region), (7) ~1088 (dominant sharp band), (8) ~1100 (shoulder/satellite band on low side of 1088), (9) ~1210, (10) ~1240 (broad structure, 1218-1254 region). Retain the residual-driven option to add an 11th component near ~1235 if a bimodal residual persists in the high-wavenumber cluster.

issues.problem: The strongest peak is under-resolved: the fit peaks too low and slightly off-center, and the residual shows a sharp derivative-like +/- oscillation (4 sign-changes, RMS/noise=268.6, peak ~1572σ).
The ~703 feature shows a systematic derivative oscillation (3 sign-changes, RMS/noise=34.7, ~217σ); the two near-coincident components (700.0 and 703.3) are not reproducing the peak apex shape.

Multiple low-lying features are under-resolved. There is a distinct small maximum near x≈142–143 that the flat near-zero baseline/fit leaves entirely uncovered, plus systematic residual structure across 160–216.

verification_iterations.fix_applied: Re-seed/retune within the locked 10-Voigt model: move peak_7 center to ~1085.4 and free its width/shape to catch the apex; straddle peak_5/peak_6 around ~703.5; relocate a low-x component (peak_1) to ~142.8 to cover the missed maximum.

issues.problem: Two clearly-real maxima are completely unmodelled: a sharp peak at x≈189–190 (~1100 counts) and a strong peak at x≈213–215 (~1900 counts). The current peak_2 is a single broad Gaussian (FWHM≈39) sitting near 203 that averages across both, leaving huge positive residuals.

verification_iterations.fix_applied: Split the broad peak_2 into two narrow components seeded at ~190 and ~214 (repurpose the near-zero peak_3), and add/sharpen an apex component at ~1085 to kill the derivative oscillation on the main band.
